author: @fl0rianr

evidence.api_compatibility: Not breaking. The endpoint now accepts one or more image[] fields instead of a single image field, but the old single-image contract is preserved (image_data fallback path retained for callers that do not use repeated fields). The /v1/images/edits OpenAPI doc in docs/api/openai.md has been updated to reflect the new behavior.
evidence.documentation: docs/api/openai.md updated: the endpoint description now says 'one or more reference images', the image parameter accepts PNG or JPEG and notes repeatable image[] fields, and the size parameter describes the new auto-dimension behavior with the 4 MP soft cap.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No evidence that a human exercised the multi-reference image editing endpoint end-to-end. The POST /v1/images/edits endpoint now accepts repeated image[] fields, auto-selects output dimensions from the first reference image, and applies a 4 MP soft cap — all user-visible behavior that should be manually verified with real images before release. Two image formats (PNG and JPEG) are parsed, which adds another dimension to test.
evidence.post_approval_commits: No commits were added after @bitgamma's approval (submitted at 2026-10-12T11:35:12Z). The merge happened at 2026-10-12T12:19:16Z with three commits in total, all preceding approval.
evidence.review: PR #3801 was reviewed by @bitgamma (theneoise, backends, benchmarking). They first requested changes on two points: (1) extract and cap the first-image size at the endpoint level rather than per-backend for coherent cross-engine behavior, and (2) add a resolution cap (they suggested 1024 area) to avoid users uploading 40 MP images that cause OOM or incoherent output. The author followed up with commit 914bbc9 (addressing a CodeRabbit-bot concern about mixed image/image[] field names) and commit c009934 (moving size extraction and capping into the /images/edits handler in server.cpp with a 4 MP default cap). @bitgamma approved the final version. No dedicated stable-diffusion or image-generation reviewer was engaged — @ramkrishna2910 covers stable diffusion in the maintainers list but was not a reviewer on this PR. The reviewer guidelines recommend having at least one reviewer with subject-area expertise.
evidence.security: No security concerns identified. The change adds PNG and JPEG header parsing for dimension extraction (no external dependency), preserves original bytes through backends without re-encoding (no new serialization path), and does not touch authentication, permissions, or credential handling.
evidence.tests: The PR author reports local testing covering server build, single/multiple reference images, explicit and original output resolution, and compatibility with GUI/GUI3. CI passes (Server Download Registry, Routing Schema, Validate New llama.cpp Release, C++ Server Build/Test/Release). However, there are no new automated unit or integration tests for the multi-reference parsing, dimension extraction, or 4 MP cap logic in the codebase diff. The CodeRabbit-bot inline comment about mixed field ordering was addressed in a follow-up commit.

maintainer_todos.text: Start the server with Flux-2-Klein-4B or SD-Turbo, send POST /v1/images/edits with two different image[] uploads and a prompt, and confirm the output is edited using both references at the auto-selected dimensions (derived from the first image, capped at 4 MP).

subject: fix(server): support multi-reference image editing (#3801)
summary: Extends the POST /v1/images/edits endpoint to accept one or more reference images (repeating image[] fields), auto-selects output dimensions from the first reference with a 4 MP soft cap, and preserves original image bytes through the SD CPP and TheNoise backends without re-encoding.
verdict_reason: All checks passed and a subject-matter reviewer approved, but no evidence that anyone manually exercised the multi-reference image editing endpoint end-to-end before merge.
